title: Tech Note: The 4DDebugLog.txt File
author: Hugo Fournier, Technical Support Manager, 4D, Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note documents the 4DDebugLog.txt low-level execution trace facility introduced in 4D 2004.3, along with a hand-rolled log rotation/archiving scheme built from a monitoring process and DELAY PROCESS polling loop. The underlying diagnostic concept (a rolling execution trace for post-mortem crash analysis) is still conceptually useful and a similar debug log mechanism has persisted in later 4D versions, but the specific command syntax (SET DATABASE PARAMETER selector 34) and the manual polling-based archiving code shown here reflect very old-school 4D idioms predating the SQL engine, Project Mode, and modern logging/monitoring tooling.
related_updates: 4D has since introduced more structured logging and debugging tools (e.g. the 4D debugger, structured log commands, and 4D Server's activity/administration logs) beyond a single flat debug text file
Later 4D releases generally favor dedicated commands and preference-based settings over manually managed SET DATABASE PARAMETER selectors for many diagnostic features
4D v11 (2007) introduced 4D's native SQL engine, part of the broader platform modernization that followed this 2006 note
